steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Capacitance C = Q/V, measured in farads (F); a capacitor stores charge on parallel plates separated by a dielectric.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The energy stored in a capacitor is E = ½CV² = ½QV.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: In an RC charging circuit, V_C rises exponentially: V_C = V_supply(1 − e^(−t/RC)).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The time constant τ = RC is the time for the capacitor to reach 63.2% of its final voltage when charging.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: A 100 μF capacitor is charged to 10 V. How much charge is stored? | Q: What is the time constant of a circuit with R = 10 kΩ and C = 20 μF? | Q: How much energy is stored in a 47 μF capacitor charged to 12 V?

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always convert units: μF to F (×10⁻⁶), mH to H (×10⁻³) before substituting into formulas. State the exponential formula before substituting values in RC circuit questions. Remember: at t = τ, charging reaches 63.2%; after 5τ it is ~99.3% charged. For energy calculations, use E = ½CV² for capacitors and E = ½LI² for inductors. Sketch the exponential charging/discharging curve to support your answer when asked to describe behaviour.
